about.title: Care and creativity have always met in Daw Mi's work.
about.body1: Her work brings together experience in healthcare, mental health, creative practice and art therapy. VetMiMi grew from a simple idea: creativity can give us another way to notice, express and reflect.
about.body2: Daw Mi is a certified art psychotherapist, transformative artist, and co-founder of The Art of Wellness at Royal North Shore Hospital in Sydney. The artworks on this site were made in these sessions.

sarah.quote: I walked in not knowing what to expect and left feeling like I had finally said something I never found words for.

faq.title: What people ask first
faq.imageAlt: A shared painting of a garden path, tree and apple, made in The Art of Wellness sessions

whatIs.a: Art psychotherapy uses the creative process — drawing, painting, collage — as a medium for self-expression and reflection. You do not need any art experience. The artwork you make is not judged; what it evokes and reveals is what matters.

draw.q: Do I need to know how to draw?
draw.a: No. You do not need to know how to draw, or make anything beautiful. Many people who come have never picked up a paintbrush. The process of making is what matters, not the result.

session.q: What does a session look like?
session.a: Sessions are 50–60 minutes, one-on-one. We begin with a brief conversation, then explore through art materials at your own pace. The way a session unfolds can be different each time.

medicare.q: Is this covered by Medicare or private health?
medicare.a: Art psychotherapy may be covered under Mental Health Care Plans with a GP referral, or through private health extras. Contact us to discuss your specific situation.

howMany.q: How many sessions will I need?
howMany.a: Some people find real value in a single session; others benefit from ongoing work over weeks or months. There is no pressure to commit beyond what feels right for you.
